messages:
maria: Quick question — onboarding BrightHealth wants BYOK in Azure Managed HSM. They want automatic rotation every 7 days and strict audit trails. What are our constraints on rotation frequency and do they need to rewrap existing envelope keys when rotating? Also their security team asked for a short validation checklist we can run.

samir: Hi @maria — short answer: we don't enforce a hard minimum rotation interval, but operationally we recommend >= 24h so caches/replication and any long-lived worker processes can observe the new key version. For Azure MHSM, rotating means creating a new key version. Envelopes encrypted with the old KEK (key-encryption-key) remain decryptable as long as the old key version is retained and our service principal still has `unwrapKey`/`get` on it. If the customer wants all ciphertext re-encrypted under the new KEK immediately you must perform a rewrap step (decrypt with old KEK, encrypt with new KEK) for stored envelopes. :information_source:

samir: Also important: for MHSM we require the following permissions for our Redwood SPN: `get`, `wrapKey`, `unwrapKey`, `sign` (if used for attestation). If they put keys in a Key Vault (non-HSM) the same wrap/unwrap perms apply but the security posture differs (HSM is preferred for BYOK).

alex: Example CLI snippets to check and grant perms (run as admin in their subscription):
```
az keyvault set-policy --name bright-mhsm --spn <REDWOOD_SPN> --key-permissions wrapKey unwrapKey get
az keyvault key list-versions --vault-name bright-mhsm --name bright-key
```
These show the key versions and add the required key permissions.

samir: For audit logging: ensure Diagnostic Settings are enabled on the Key Vault and pointed to a Log Analytics workspace or Event Hub we can consume. We look for `Microsoft.KeyVault/Keys/Unwrap/action`, `Wrap/action`, `Get/key` events. Also insist they enable soft-delete + purge protection on the vault so rotated old key versions aren't accidentally purged during troubleshooting.

alex: Example diag create (customer side):
```
az monitor diagnostic-settings create --resource /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/bright-mhsm --workspace <log-analytics-id> --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]'
```

jen: Thanks — I'll confirm with their infra team that they can grant the SPN and enable diagnostic settings. Also will check whether BrightHealth wants immediate rewrap or prefer gradual re-encryption.

maria: Great — action items: (1) @jen validate SPN and diag settings, (2) I will draft a short KB checklist for BYOK MHSM onboarding that includes exact permission commands, diagnostic events to look for, and recommended rotation workflow (reliant on key versions vs mandatory rewrap).

kms-bot: Tip: use our internal validator `kms-validate` to test wrap/unwrap after SPN policy changes: `kms-validate --provider azure --vault bright-mhsm --key bright-key --spn <REDWOOD_SPN>`. Returns pass/fail and a short event log. Link: https://redwood.internal/kms/bindings/docs/onboard-byok 

samir: One more security note: if they insist on 7-day automatic rotation via a managed policy, ensure you have a fallback plan in case rotation fails (we can opt to keep a short grace period where both versions are accepted). We'll add that to the KB.

maria: Perfect, thanks everyone. I'll post the KB draft here once done and tag @samir for review.
